message.content: {"caption":"Two-panel point chart comparing memory-quality scores across six methods for two model backbones.","description":"The chart has two vertically stacked panels, each with Memory Quality (MQ) on the y-axis and six methods on the x-axis: LangMem, A-Mem, Mem0, Mem0^g, AgeMem-noRL, and AgeMem. The upper panel is labeled “(a) Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct” and spans approximately 0.3–0.6 MQ; the lower panel is labeled “(b) Qwen3-4B-Instruct” and spans approximately 0.4–0.7 MQ. Blue circles denote Baselines, red stars denote AgeMem, and a gray dashed horizontal line with a light gray band denotes Avg. Baseline. Thin stems connect the plotted markers to that reference level. The average-baseline line reads at about 0.47 in the upper panel and 0.51 in the lower panel. In both panels, AgeMem is highlighted by a red rectangular outline and has the highest score. In the upper panel, baseline scores rise from LangMem through Mem0, then decline at Mem0^g and AgeMem-noRL; the red AgeMem star is above all of them. In the lower panel, A-Mem is the highest baseline, followed by declining scores through Mem0, Mem0^g, and AgeMem-noRL; AgeMem is above all baselines.
